To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 2 different weight tablets of an OC with the same hormonal contents are bioequivalent to each other and to the same OC in solution.
the two tablets of differing weights of an oral contraceptive were bioequivalent with respect to the total absorption of NET and EE2.
the two different weight tablets of an OC are bioequivalent to each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the bioequivalence of two formulations of the same hormonal content, one of which has a lower weight.
the bioequivalence of two different weight tablets of an OC, with the same hormonal components and with the same total weight of active ingredient.
the bioequivalence of two tablets with the same content of NET and EE2 but with different weights and the same solution of the components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two formulations are bioequivalent.
the two tablets are bioequivalent to each other and to the solution with respect to NET and EE2.
the two tablets of different weights are bioequivalent with each other and with the solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 50 mg tablets were bioequivalent to 100 mg tablets and to the solution.
the two tablets were not significantly different with regard to the parameters measured.
the two different weight tablets of the same hormonal content were bioequivalent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the same formulation for both tablets, but the weight of the tablets can be different.
bioequivalence of two different tablets with the same active pharmaceutical ingredients can be demonstrated by comparing them with a solution of the same active ingredients.
the use of a single dose of 100 mg of NET and 0.03 mg of EE2 in the same tablet is not a good idea.
